evidence: The original entry said the hold forces 'every concurrent open in every process into the write-nothing fallback', but write opens set BackOff/FailOnJournalLockTimeout and fail after ~30s; 45a6049 rewrote the changelog, LockDoltJournalExclusive doc and takeUserSnapshot comment to state the two arms.
guidance_note: When documenting a lock's effect on its contenders, enumerate each contender class (read open, write open) and state its outcome separately instead of generalizing from the one you measured.

evidence: The 45a6049 CHANGELOG diff shows the three prior Unreleased entries still described the engine slot, 'remains as the outer serializer', and the 'workspace+engine lock pair', all false once this PR deleted the engine lock; the fix rewrote all three.
guidance_note: When a PR retires a named mechanism, grep the Unreleased changelog and docs for that mechanism's name and reconcile every hit in the same commit.

evidence: The original openStoreConnection pinged every access mode, so an engineRead open under a snapshot's held LOCK would mint a permanent read-only engine before the commit-lock wait and fail migrate; 45a6049 gates the ping on access == engineWrite.
guidance_note: Before making a lazy resource eager, trace every caller's sequence after construction (here OpenForRead's migrate under the commit lock) to confirm none depended on the deferral.

evidence: acquireStoreLock MkdirAll+O_CREATEs the lock path, so pointing it at Dolt's own .dolt/noms/LOCK would fabricate the tree on an uninitialized workspace; 45a6049 stats the noms dir first and refuses on ENOENT, with a test that nothing is created.
guidance_note: When reusing a lock helper on a file another program owns, check whether the helper's create-if-missing behavior is valid for that file before calling it.

evidence: The original reconnect opened lazily, so contention surfaced raw at the next query rather than through wrapEngineOpenContention; instead of a second classifier at the mutation boundary, 45a6049 pings after prev.Close() inside reconnect and wraps through the existing enforcer, which keeps one mapping site.
guidance_note: When adding an error-classifying wrapper, list every site that can produce the wrapped error (including lazy re-opens) and route each through it.

evidence: 45a6049 changed connectionRotator to take ctx specifically so cancellation could escape reconnect's ping, but only updated existing test closures to ignore ctx; no test exercised the new cancellation path until 93a3b14 added a blocking-rotator test.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a signature to enable a new behavior, add the test that exercises that behavior in the same commit, not just the compile fixes to existing callers.

evidence: F3's lazy-read fix only covered the reader-waits-behind-snapshot ordering; when the reader wins the commit race while the snapshot holds LOCK, the lazy engine still resolves read-only and migrate fails. The agent's rejection of the suggested in-hold reopen is sound: the snapshot keeps LOCK while waiting on commit, so any reopen meets the same held LOCK.
guidance_note: When fixing a lock-interleaving bug, enumerate both orderings of the two acquirers and state the outcome of each before declaring the fix complete.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 93a3b14 only added a retry test and OpenForRead classification; the missing ErrWorkspaceBusy sentinel came from the original PR's replacement of the engine-lock wrapper with wrapEngineOpenContention. 40105f4 makes the wrapper carry both ErrWorkspaceBusy and nbs.ErrDatabaseLocked and tests it through real OpenSync.
guidance_note: When deleting a mechanism, list every sentinel its error wrapper carried and grep for consumers that errors.Is on those sentinels, so the replacement keeps them.

evidence: 93a3b14 (F7's fix) added the isManifestReadOnlyError classification in OpenForRead with no test; 40105f4 added TestOpenForReadPendingMigrationUnderJournalHolder, which seeds one migration behind, holds LOCK, and asserts the guidance and the healed retry.
guidance_note: When a fix depends on an existing predicate matching a new error path, write the test that proves the match in the fix commit rather than assuming it.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the journal hold in takeUserSnapshot is original-PR code, not 93a3b14. The mandatory LockFileEx conflict with a second-handle read is plausible, but the claim that closing the copy's handle would release the lock is doubtful, because Windows byte-range locks belong to the handle that took them; skipping the contentless LOCK file is cheap and correct regardless.
guidance_note: When a new lock is held on a file inside a tree another step walks, check each platform backend's lock semantics (mandatory vs advisory) against that walk.

evidence: 45a6049 (F2's fix) rewrote this exact declaration entry to drop the engine slot but kept 'the commit lock's O_EXCL create ... predate it (il18.2/.4)', which the same Unreleased section's commit-lock entry contradicts; a72ea30 removed it.
guidance_note: When reconciling a changelog entry with the release's final state, check every claim in the sentence you are editing against the other entries, not only the claim the reviewer named.

guidance_note: When adding a relative cross-reference (above/below) in a doc, check the target's actual position in the file before committing.

guidance_note: When a fix accepts a new user-visible failure mode as a deliberate trade, record it in the changelog in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the claim/clear mechanism is links-sync-pgct.12's and was not touched by a72ea30 (only the comment's wording was edited in the original PR). The interleaving is real but not silent, since every non-push clear writes a failed push-outcome record; the agent declined the mechanism change and fixed the comment's 'Covered, by construction' overclaim. The law token decorates an argument that stands on its mechanics alone.
guidance_note: When rewording a proof comment in passing, re-check its unconditional claims against the code's failure paths rather than only swapping the mechanism name.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the DoltJournalLockPath 'ONE HOME exception' comment is original-PR text, not changed by a72ea30 (a CHANGELOG-only commit). 'Every acquirer holds the workspace lock' is false for a non-lit dolt process, which engineOpenRetryMaxElapsed's own doc names as a holder.
guidance_note: Before writing a universal ('every acquirer') in a doc comment, check it against the holders the same package already enumerates elsewhere.

narrative: The PR retired lit's engine lock in favor of Dolt's own journal LOCK. Each round reviewed only 3 scopes before the time budget ran out, so original-code findings (F8, F10, F14, F15) kept surfacing late. Rounds 1 and 3 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings: F5's ctx change shipped untested (F6); F3's lazy-read fix covered only one lock ordering (F7), and F7's fix then shipped without a test (F9) or a changelog note (F13); F2's changelog reconciliation left a stale claim and wrong-direction pointers (F11, F12). The agent's technical judgment was strong throughout, including correctly declining the reopen suggestion on F7 and the mechanism change on F14.
guidance_observations: Fix commits repeatedly shipped behavior changes without the test or changelog line that the next round then demanded; bundling test + doc with each behavior change would have removed most of rounds 1 and 3.
A lock-ordering change needs both interleavings of each acquirer pair enumerated up front; the F3 to F7 chain came from fixing one ordering at a time.
The reviewer's per-round scope cap means a clean round is not coverage; original-PR defects (lost ErrWorkspaceBusy sentinel, Windows mandatory lock) appeared only in rounds 2 and 4.
